Confirmed by driving ?state=loading and ?state=full in chromium at 1440 and diffing the two DOMs: the skeleton's marks are the real marks, pixel for pixel. All twelve .sk-wrap .bar carry --h 42/25/50/33/58/42/67/50/50/67/42/100 - seven distinct heights, exactly the list the seat names - and their boxes are identical to the full state's to the pixel (593,401,22x71 ... 1195,304,22x168). All nine .sk-wrap .dot carry the real ages as --x (4.44, 6.67, 11.11, 13.33, 20, 24.44, 42.22, 51.11, 91.11), and at 390 deswarm stacks them into the real swarm (rows 0,1,0,1,0,1,0,0,0). The geometry argument holds: .plot is a fixed 168px box (lately.html:236), .cols is absolutely positioned (237) and .bar height is a percentage of a full-height .colw (242), so the varying heights buy zero layout stability; .strip is a fixed 92px and .dot is absolutely positioned by --x, same story. The gate's four skeleton assertions (interaction-check.mjs:374-378) measure card count, hero height, card height and section count; none reads a magnitude, so this is not a restatement of anything already proven. And it is legible, not theoretical: 22px columns of rgba(17,17,17,0.03) on white read plainly in shots/light-loading--1440x960.png, with the tallest column unmistakably the last one.

The seat under-scoped its own finding, and its fix inherits the gap. Three further channels publish real magnitudes and the proposed fix touches none of them. (1) .sk-wrap .bar-val sits at bottom:calc(var(--h)*1% + 6px) with --h:100 (lately.html:291, 716); set only the bars to 46 and that chip strands 97px above its own column at the top of the plot - the exact geometric drift this skeleton exists to prevent. (2) .sk-wrap .record-tag sits at bottom:calc(var(--r)*1%) with --r:67, painting the previous-best ceiling, even though .record itself is visibility:hidden at line 460 - so the tag already floats labelling a rule that is not there, and after the seat's fix it would float above every flattened column. (3) .sk-wrap .meter i keeps transform:scaleX(var(--f)) at the real fractions 0.333/0.222/0.111/0, rendering 57px/38px/19px/0px wash fills - the last of which is a zero-width mark standing for a number nobody has read, which is the honest-degradation contract's own failure mode. The last bar also keeps .bar.part's mask-image and square corners (computed: linear-gradient(to top,#000 72%,transparent), border-radius 0), so the skeleton draws the partial-week treatment of a week it has not read either.

Severity 'defect' is right and I am not correcting it upward: the marks are true, so the surface asserts nothing untrue about the reading, and a reader who waits sees the identical shape. What is wrong is the state's claim about itself - and the real cost is at port time, where this branch cannot be built from a model that has no data. That is a build, not a redesign: the values are the only thing being changed, and no box, wrap point or column moves.
sharpenedFix: Neutralise every magnitude in one pass immediately after root.innerHTML = VIEW[state]() (lately.html:1012) and BEFORE deswarm runs, rather than in the later strip pass at 1144 - then nothing downstream needs re-running. For state === 'loading', over root.querySelector('.sk-wrap'): set --h to 46 on every .bar AND on every .bar-val, so the chip moves with its column instead of stranding; remove the 'part' class from the last .bar so it loses the open-top mask and square corners, which are a treatment of a week nobody has read; set --f to one neutral fraction (0.4) on every .meter i and remove the 'zero' class, so no meter paints a zero-width mark for an unknown; add .record-tag beside .record in the visibility:hidden rule at line 460, since the rule it labels is already hidden and the tag otherwise floats alone at the true previous-best level; and rewrite every .dot's --x to an even (i + 0.5) / n spread. Leave .strip-scale span --x alone - those already sit at fixed fractions of the axis and encode nothing. Then add gate assertions that actually bite, because the four existing ones cannot see this: in the loading state, every .sk-wrap .bar shares one --h; every .sk-wrap .meter i shares one --f; no .sk-wrap element carries 'part' or 'zero'; and the ordered set of .sk-wrap .dot --x values is NOT equal to the full state's.
breaks: Nothing in layout. .plot is a fixed 168px and .strip a fixed 92px; .bar is a percentage height inside a full-height .colw; .bar-val, .record-tag and .dot are absolutely positioned. So no reflow, no scroll shift and no focus move - which is also why the seat's premise that the varying values buy no stability is correct. Re-measure after it lands: (1) the four skeleton assertions at interaction-check.mjs:374-378 - card count and card height are untouched, but the hero contains the chart, so confirm the skeleton hero still matches the real hero within 8px at 390/768/1280/1440 once the 'part' class is dropped, since that class controls the last bar's mask and radius; (2) deswarm at lately.html:1047 now runs on evenly spread dots and will return row 0 for all nine at every width, so any assertion that counts skeleton rows or measures loading-state dot hit targets must be re-run at 390, where the real data currently produces two rows; (3) run both gates end to end, not just the skeleton block - the change edits shared .bar/.bar-val/.meter/.dot behaviour by class and a mis-scoped selector would reach the full state silently, where --h and --f are load-bearing; and (4) re-shoot shots/light-loading--1440x960.png and its dark twin, since the published frame is the evidence this was fixed.
